name: Blueprint II
description: All JetBlue blue, nose to tail, fin, engines and winglets, drawn over in thin white and coloured line art like a blueprint of the aircraft: the cabin's floor line, frames and doors, seats, bags, bikes and other things carried, in outline. 'jetBlue' in large white letters over the forward windows. The fin carries a few thin white construction lines along its leading edge and tip.

sources.title: JetBlue: Returning to the Runway: JetBlue Debuts Blueprint II on an Airbus A220 (Business Wire, 2026-05-15)
sources.note: Blueprint II in scheduled service on a new A220 from May 2026; a reimagining of the 2017 E190 Blueprint.

blue.name: JetBlue blue (darker in shade, #4263B3 in sun on the fin)

linePink.name: pink linework (the surfboard, the bike's frame)

logos.description: The blueprint line art over the whole fuselage: a thin white floor line under the windows nose to tail, frames and doors in outline, and below them outlines of seats, bags, bikes, musical instruments and other things carried, mostly white with touches of pink, red and orange. Linework only: the fuselage stays blue.

The fin's construction lines: a white line curving up the rear of the fin to the tip, a white line along the tip, and a thin cyan and a thin lavender-pink line rising side by side through the middle of the fin.
A small US flag ahead of the registration over the rear windows.

titles.style: The jetBlue wordmark, large, in white over the forward windows.

notes: Measured on N3308J's left side, 2026-07-08 (two photos a moment apart, the only open ones). The scheme's colour field is one blue; everything else is linework, described as a logo (docs/LOGOS.md) and not drawn as areas. 'Blueprint II' (small white script under the cockpit) and the registration aren't drawn. The first Blueprint (E190 N304JB, 2017) left with JetBlue's E190s, all retired by 9 Sep 2025.
